quickAnswer: With three full days in Shanghai, group the old-city sights and the Bund on Day 1, walk the former French Concession and central neighbourhoods on Day 2, then use Day 3 for Pudong plus a museum, riverfront, or carefully chosen day trip. Shanghai is compact compared with Beijing, but transfers, queues, heat, rain, and large museums can still make an overfilled plan tiring. Check live opening hours and reservation rules, save every destination in Chinese, and keep one indoor alternative for poor weather. Use the opening-day and museum-venue checks below before fixing the order.
gardenNote: Start in the Yuyuan Garden and City God Temple area after checking the garden's live opening, ticket, and entry arrangements. Go earlier if you prefer quieter lanes. If this falls on a Monday, use the alternative order below rather than assuming the ticketed garden will open.
museumNote: Choose the actual museum venue from the comparison above. Allow its transfer and visit to replace a substantial part of the Pudong day instead of squeezing it between several skyline stops.

faqs.question: Can I visit Yu Garden on a Monday?
faqs.answer: The historic garden normally closes on Mondays, except national holidays. Use the Monday alternative above and check official notices for your date; garden access is separate from the surrounding area.

faqs.question: Which Shanghai Museum should I choose for permanent collections?
faqs.answer: Choose Shanghai Museum East under the current arrangement. The People's Square venue is dedicated to an Americas exhibition from July 9, 2026 to November 14, 2027. Recheck the operator's programme before visiting.

faqs.question: Is Shanghai Museum East open on Tuesday?
faqs.answer: East normally closes on Tuesdays, except national holidays. The People's Square venue usually closes on Mondays, so choose the venue and programme before setting the day.
